summary.headline: Black Box targets INR12,000 crore organic plus INR6,000 crore inorganic revenue by FY30 (~$2bn), with 10% EBITDA margin; order book ~$800m.
summary.overview: This was a Capital Markets Day held June 1, 2026 (transcript filed June 7), not a quarterly earnings call, so no Q4 FY26 quarterly P&L was presented beyond FY26 annual figures. Management said the turnaround is complete and set a FY30 target of INR12,000 crore organic revenue (~$1.3bn, 17% CAGR from ~INR6,000 crore) plus ~INR6,000 crore (~$0.7bn) from acquisitions. FY26 EBITDA was INR570 crore at a 9% margin, up from 4.3% in FY23, and the order book reached ~$800m. Growth is pinned on hyperscale data centre fit-out, enterprise GSI services, the TPS products business (~$90m to $200m) and rest-of-world, including India.

financial_highlights.change: Expanded by 470 bps (as stated; likely margin expansion context)
From INR269 crore and 4.3% margin in FY23
Up from ~$500m; ~60% growth cited; $1bn booked in FY26

financial_highlights.value: Over 9x growth in last three years

financial_highlights.change: Total capital raised ~INR600 crore in the period

financial_highlights.value: Receivables up ~INR580 crore QoQ; payables up ~INR300 crore; receivable days ~90+ vs 60-75 normal
financial_highlights.change: Driven by 38:62 revenue skew to March quarter

segments.name: Hyperscale data centre / GSI
segments.commentary: Data centre share of order book ~25%, guided to rise to 35-40% in coming quarters. Seven dedicated sites for one hyperscaler (three more allocated); GSI headcount ~1,500, with 400 in data centre practice and 2,100 hires planned in 12 months, mostly in the US.

segments.name: Technology Product Solutions (TPS)
segments.commentary: Current business ~$90m, targeted at ~$200m by FY30 with ~40% gross margin and a 10% EBITDA target. Seven verticals addressed, ~$3bn TAM; R&D in Bangalore and Limerick, Ireland; flagship product line Emerald.

segments.name: India / Rest of World
segments.commentary: India is 6-7% of revenue (~$50m), targeted at 8-10% of a $2bn business (~$200m). India is a low-margin geography per management; 300+ partnerships and 17 offices / 35 delivery centres cited.

segments.name: Financial services (anchor client)
segments.commentary: A large US bank client has been served for 27 years at ~$100m annual spend, ~$1bn lifetime revenue crossed in the last 10 years, 68% growth since 2016.

guidance_outlook: FY30 target: INR12,000 crore organic revenue (~$1.3bn, ~17% CAGR) plus ~INR6,000 crore inorganic (~$0.7bn), totaling ~INR18,000 crore (~$2bn). Computed at INR95/$.
EBITDA margin: 10% overall target, reached in FY27 per management (9% currently); FY30 EBITDA margin target of 10%+.
Order book expected to reach $1.3-1.4bn by March 2027 (guided 50%+ growth in FY27 bookings); average order age 15-18 months.

Acquisitions: ~$200-250m of revenue acquired per year, targeting 2-5% EBITDA margin targets bought at 6-8x and turned to 9-10% in 90-120 days; 70% upfront, 30% earn-out. Brazil (2S) acquisition recently announced.
Debt-to-equity could rise to ~1:1 after the acquisition programme; otherwise debt to stay broadly flat with internal accruals.
capex_capacity: Data centre workforce: 2,100 hires planned in next 12 months (mostly US) to go from ~4,000 total employees to ~7,000.
GCC in Bengaluru to grow from ~600 to ~1,000 people.
Centralised resource management in Plano, Texas; estimating tools Accubid and P6 Primavera; separate project controls team.
Training: 600 people trained on AI; 36 hours of learning per person per year vs 28-hour industry average; 1,500 certifications in data centre business.
Capital allocation priorities: people and training, AI-enabled platforms, working capital, and acquisitions in Europe, APAC, India and Latin America.
demand_pricing: Management says demand outweighs supply in data centre work; prices have 'considerably increased', with cost increases passed through; margins claimed to improve modestly with execution.
Mike Carney stated no business is won on price; win depends on execution and relationships.
Hyperscaler data centre contracts: mainly time-and-materials / design-build; ~25% of project value is unknown at outset; change orders agreed, e.g. ~$2.5m change orders on a $10m initial scope.
US skilled labour market is constrained; inflation expected. Talent on Tap programme trains trade-school hires (~3 weeks) to address it.
Management claims ~0.2% share of the $200bn networking and connectivity opportunity; India data centre market from 1.3 GW to 8 GW (42% CAGR), India IT $171bn (9.2% CAGR per Gartner).

qa_highlights.question: Margin trajectory for non-TPS businesses, and how acquisitions will be funded (~$200m a year).
qa_highlights.answer: Target is 10% EBITDA across all businesses; management expects to reach 9% to 10% in FY27 with scale. Acquisitions funded mainly by internal accruals plus some debt; ~$200-250m of revenue acquired per year.

qa_highlights.question: Share of hyperscaler exposure in order book and margin difference vs enterprise.
qa_highlights.answer: Data centres ~25% of order book, rising to 35-40%. Margins are stated as not varying by customer type; India is a low-margin geography and data centre operators/multi-tenants carry higher margins than general contractors.

qa_highlights.question: Contract structure for data centre projects (time-based vs fixed price).
qa_highlights.answer: Mix of annuity contracts, fixed-price small projects and cost-plus for large multi-year projects; management says 15-20% of projects are expected to convert to annuity as the business scales to $2bn.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital days rising and receivable outlook.
qa_highlights.answer: The March quarter revenue skew (62% in March vs 38% in first two months) raised receivables by ~INR580 crore; management expects receivable days to revert to 60-75 from ~90+ as the skew normalises to 45:55.

qa_highlights.question: Hiring split by geography and rupee sensitivity.
qa_highlights.answer: The 4,000 headcount is ~2,000 US, ~1,200 India (500-550 India business, balance GCC), ~300 Europe, ~400 Latin America; hiring is revenue-based and the US accounts for most growth. Plan computed at INR95/$; currency moves affect INR revenue, margin percentages unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Risks to the FY30 plan.
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited talent and attrition, unforeseen events and geopolitics; said currency is naturally hedged (earn and spend in same currency) and the main risk is project execution.

risks_watch: Execution on large, multi-year data centre projects where ~25% of value is unknown at start and scope changes are common.
Talent: 2,100 US hires in 12 months in a constrained labour market; wage inflation and attrition.
Working capital: receivable days at ~90+ and the March-quarter revenue skew; watch normalisation toward 60-75 days.
Acquisition integration and the INR6,000 crore inorganic target, funded partly with debt; D/E could rise to ~1:1.
Tax rate normalising from ~10% to 18-20% after about two years, which will weigh on PAT.
Order book conversion: target of $1.3-1.4bn by March 2027 and new hyperscaler wins.
summary.management_tone: Highly confident and promotional, with aspirational targets described as a 'dream' and 'plan A'. Specific numbers are given for FY30 and order book, but several claims (market sizes, share, margins) are loosely supported and the Q&A on margin, tax and funding was answered in detail.
key_quotes: So, this is our organic plan, primarily the aspiration to go to INR12,000 crores from current INR6,000 crores, almost like doubling that to a $1.3 billion revenue.
We are expecting that when we end this fiscal year, which is March '27, our order book will remain in the range of probably $1.3 -1.4 billion.
Without a hyperscaler being there, it won't happen, because they are the anchor tenants for most of the GPU data centers.
The focus now is the execution.
